solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Some attitude: let everyone strike

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone's attitude is so bad they want everyone to go on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike text, or strike it out, is to cross it out and remove it from a document.

clue.text: Refusals of Pope, finally, to visit Craggy Island

indicators.note: a letter that visits a word goes inside it, so it is placed within the jumbled letters
craggy means rugged and broken up, so the letters of the next word are broken up and rearranged
finally points to the closing letter of the word Pope

explanation.surface: The Pope turns down invitations to Craggy Island, the remote setting of the sitcom Father Ted.
explanation.walkthrough: Craggy Island is the parish in the Irish sitcom Father Ted, the puzzle's theme. 'Craggy' rearranges ISLAND to DNIALS, and 'to visit' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A denial is a refusal of a request, so denials and refusals are plural synonyms.

clue.text: Sign left one bishop really angry, to start with

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: to start with picks the opening letter of each of the words really and angry

explanation.surface: A road sign that told a bishop to go left made him furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra, the scales, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Tune Mrs Doyle ruined to a great extent

indicators.note: a ruined tune has been wrecked, so the letters of these words are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: Mrs Doyle, the housekeeper in Father Ted, has badly mangled a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Doyle is the tea-pushing housekeeper in the sitcom Father Ted.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremendously is an adverb of degree meaning hugely, a phrase-for-word synonym of to a great extent.

clue.text: Work, going forward and back, for counterpart

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: the work is read forwards and then backwards, so a second copy is turned round

explanation.surface: A job that keeps lurching forwards and backwards is matched against its opposite number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going forward and back' means the same two letters are written once forwards, then again reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppo is British informal for a colleague or opposite number, someone who mirrors your role.

clue.text: Strange priests carry on

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of order, so the letters of the next word are disordered

explanation.surface: Some odd clergymen keep going regardless, as the priests of Father Ted do.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist is to continue steadily despite obstacles, which is what carrying on means.

clue.text: Lascivious looks Dougal gets every so often

indicators.note: every so often picks letters at regular intervals, here every second one starting from the second

explanation.surface: Father Dougal, the dim young priest in Father Ted, occasionally receives leering glances.
explanation.walkthrough: Dougal is Father Dougal McGuire of Father Ted.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogles are leering, lustful stares, exactly lascivious looks.

clue.text: Put out tabloid newspaper: about time

indicators.note: the newspaper goes about, or around, the letter for time

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid daily newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put out a tabloid paper story about time.
explanation.definitionFit: Put out can mean knocked unconscious, as when a blow stuns someone.

clue.text: Father Ted in a curious yellow

indicators.note: curious means strange or peculiar, so these letters are put into a peculiar new order

explanation.surface: Father Ted, the sitcom priest, appears in a strange yellow outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yellow' looks like a colour describing the costume, but it is the definition in its sense of cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly, and fainthearted means lacking courage.

clue.text: Name Old Boy in case most virtuous

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for Old Boy, a former pupil of a school
lest is an old conjunction meaning in case

explanation.surface: A former pupil is named, just in case, as the most upright of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble describes high moral character, so the superlative noblest means the most upright or virtuous.

clue.text: Trouble acquiring voting system within a month

indicators.note: the word for trouble acquires, or takes in, the voting system letters

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
PR stands for proportional representation, a voting system

explanation.surface: A dispute over adopting a new voting system rumbles on for a month.
explanation.definitionFit: April is the fourth month of the calendar year.

clue.text: Willing maiden grabbed by anonymous Greek hero

indicators.note: the willing-plus-maiden letters are grabbed and held inside the abbreviation for anonymous

parts.note: game means willing, as in game for anything
M is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A willing young woman is carried off by an unnamed hero of Greek legend.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, abbreviated M.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon, king of Mycenae, led the Greek army against Troy in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: One's holding loud objections

indicators.note: the letters for one's hold the loud letter between them

parts.note: one is I, so one's (one is) gives I plus S
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: Someone is voicing loud objections.
explanation.definitionFit: Ifs, as in ifs and buts, are reservations or conditions raised against a plan.

clue.text: Withdraw from paradise, briefly after a moment

indicators.note: after says the shortened paradise word comes after the moment

parts.note: sec, short for second, is a moment

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: Eden is the biblical garden of paradise

explanation.surface: Someone leaves paradise after only a brief moment there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word, and 'a moment' is easily read as the start of the definition, but it supplies the letters that come first.
explanation.definitionFit: To secede is for a member or region to formally withdraw from a union or federation.

clue.text: Black distillate company placed on communion table

indicators.note: in a down answer the company letters are placed on top of the table word

parts.note: the altar is the table used for communion in church

explanation.surface: A firm puts a black liquid on the church's communion table.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal tar is the thick black liquid distilled from coal, used in soaps and road surfaces.

clue.text: Beat with right hand? Dreadful myth

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hand, as on a watch

indicators.note: dreadful means awful, so the letters of the following word are made into a mess

explanation.surface: A drummer keeps time with the right hand, but the legend about it is awful.
explanation.definitionFit: A beat in music is the regular pulse or rhythm of a piece.

clue.text: Mass, I bet, is a blunder

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics
a stake is a sum bet on an outcome

explanation.surface: I bet Mass is a blunder, says a sceptic in a Catholic sitcom.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake is an error, which is what a blunder is.

clue.text: Cuppa from Peg, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is identified by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a tee is a small peg on which a golf ball is placed

explanation.surface: A cup of tea is served by someone called Peg, as Mrs Doyle might do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peg' looks like a name, but is a golf tee.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuppa is British informal for a cup of tea.

clue.text: Actor's article's on how play begins

indicators.note: in a down answer the article letters sit on top of the next part

parts.note: the is the definite article, so article's (article is) gives THE plus S

indicators.note: begins takes the opening letter of the word play

explanation.surface: An actor gives an opinion on how a play ought to open.
explanation.definitionFit: Thesp, short for thespian, is a jokey informal name for an actor.

clue.text: Frees one in Calais? He's crossing meadows

indicators.note: the words for he's cross, or follow on from, the meadows

parts.note: un is the French word for one, and Calais is in France
a lea is a meadow, so leas are meadows
taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A man in Calais walks across fields and sets someone free.
explanation.definitionFit: To unleash is to release from a leash or restraint, so unleashes means frees.

clue.text: Idle head one can toast

definitions.meaning: to idle is to laze about, doing nothing
in British slang your head or brain
a ... of bread is something that can be sliced and toasted

explanation.surface: A lazy boss is someone you could raise a glass to.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaf means to laze, is slang for the head, and is a bread you toast: three senses.

clue.text: It follows chicken: empty cage

parts.note: a hen is a female chicken

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its outside letters, the middle removed

explanation.surface: A chicken comes along after its cage has been emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: Hence means therefore, introducing a conclusion that it follows from what came before.

clue.text: Praise, employing some pretext, oligarch

indicators.note: employing some says only some of the letters of the following words are used, as a hidden run

explanation.surface: An oligarch is praised on some flimsy excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly and enthusiastically.

clue.text: One feels insect repelled girl

parts.note: an ant is an insect

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the girl's name is turned back to front

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An insect drove off a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is an insect's feeler, so it is one that feels its surroundings.

clue.text: Leave Father Jack in the end holding last of liquor

indicators.note: the father-and-end letters hold the final letter of liquor between them

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: in the end picks the closing letter of the word Jack
last of picks the final letter of the word liquor

explanation.surface: Father Jack, the drunken old priest of Father Ted, finally clings to the last of the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Jack Hackett is the hard-drinking priest in Father Ted.
explanation.definitionFit: To park is to leave a vehicle, or anything, in a place for a time.

clue.text: Commercial at this point getting stick

parts.note: an ad is a commercial, an advertisement
here means at this point or place

explanation.surface: An advert at this point is getting criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting stick' reads as being criticised, but 'stick' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast or cling to a surface.
